M.6.RP.A.3.cc_advanced: I can choose a table, tape diagram, double number line or equation to solve multi-step ratio, rate, percent and unit conversion problems, and explain why my method works.
M.6.RP.A.3.cc_at_target: I can use tables, diagrams and unit rates to solve ratio problems, find a percent of a number, find the whole from a part and percent, and convert units. Example: 30% of 50 = 30/100 × 50 = 15.
M.6.RP.A.3.cc_approaching: I can complete a table of equivalent ratios and find a unit rate with simple whole numbers when I have a model or a worked example to follow.
M.6.RP.A.3.cc_emerging: I can use objects or pictures to show a ratio, such as 2 red cubes for every 3 blue cubes, with help from my teacher.
M.6.RP.A.3.ee_at_target: I can show a simple ratio relationship using objects or pictures.

M.6.NS.B.4.cc_advanced: I can use GCF and LCM to solve real-world problems, such as sharing items into equal groups or finding when events repeat, and explain which one I need and why.
M.6.NS.B.4.cc_at_target: I can find the GCF of two numbers up to 100 and the LCM of two numbers up to 12, and use the GCF to rewrite a sum. Example: 36 + 8 = 4(9 + 2).
M.6.NS.B.4.cc_approaching: I can list factors or multiples of two small numbers and find a common factor or common multiple when I use a factor list or hundreds chart.
M.6.NS.B.4.cc_emerging: I can find factor pairs of a small number using arrays or multiplication facts with support.

M.6.NS.C.8.cc_advanced: I can solve real-world problems on a coordinate plane in all four quadrants, such as finding distances on a map, and explain how I used absolute value.
M.6.NS.C.8.cc_at_target: I can graph points in all four quadrants and use coordinates and absolute value to find the distance between points that share an x or y coordinate. Example: (2, 3) to (2, -4) is 3 + 4 = 7 units.
M.6.NS.C.8.cc_approaching: I can graph points in all four quadrants and count the distance between two points on the same line using the grid.
M.6.NS.C.8.cc_emerging: I can plot and name points with whole number coordinates in the first quadrant with support.
M.6.NS.C.8.ee_at_target: I can use positive and negative numbers to describe opposite amounts, like temperatures above and below zero.

M.6.EE.A.4.cc_advanced: I can create my own pairs of equivalent expressions and explain, using properties of operations, why they are equal for every value of the variable.
M.6.EE.A.4.cc_at_target: I can tell when two expressions are equivalent because they give the same value for any number I substitute. Example: y + y + y and 3y are equivalent.
M.6.EE.A.4.cc_approaching: I can substitute a few numbers into two expressions to check if they give the same value, using a table or a model.
M.6.EE.A.4.cc_emerging: I can show that two number expressions are equal, such as 3 + 3 + 3 and 3 × 3, using objects or drawings.

M.6.EE.B.8.cc_advanced: I can write inequalities for real-world limits, show the solutions on a number line, and explain why there are infinitely many solutions.
M.6.EE.B.8.cc_at_target: I can write an inequality like x > c or x < c for a real-world condition and show its solutions on a number line. Example: "more than 5 people" is x > 5.
M.6.EE.B.8.cc_approaching: I can match a simple situation to an inequality and show it on a number line using an open or closed circle with support.
M.6.EE.B.8.cc_emerging: I can compare two numbers using the symbols > and < with a number line.

M.6.G.A.3.cc_advanced: I can use coordinates to draw polygons and find side lengths to solve real-world problems, such as finding the perimeter of a garden on a grid.
M.6.G.A.3.cc_at_target: I can draw a polygon on the coordinate plane from its vertices and find the length of sides that share an x or y coordinate. Example: (1, 2) to (5, 2) is 4 units.
M.6.G.A.3.cc_approaching: I can plot given vertices and join them to make a polygon, and count grid units to find the length of a horizontal or vertical side.
M.6.G.A.3.cc_emerging: I can plot points in the first quadrant and connect them in order with help.

M.6.SP.A.3.cc_advanced: I can compare two data sets using a measure of center and a measure of variation and explain what each number tells me about the data.
M.6.SP.A.3.cc_at_target: I can explain that a measure of center (like the mean or median) gives one typical value for a data set, and a measure of variation tells how spread out the values are.
M.6.SP.A.3.cc_approaching: I can find a typical value of a small data set and say whether the values are close together or spread out, using a dot plot.
M.6.SP.A.3.cc_emerging: I can order a small set of numbers and find the middle one with support.

M.7.RP.A.2.cc_advanced: I can decide if real-world relationships are proportional, write equations like y = kx, and explain what points such as (0, 0) and (1, r) mean in the situation.
M.7.RP.A.2.cc_at_target: I can test if a relationship is proportional using a table or graph, find the constant of proportionality, and write an equation. Example: $3 per item means t = 3n.
M.7.RP.A.2.cc_approaching: I can use a table of equivalent ratios to find the unit rate and tell if the graph is a straight line through (0, 0) with support.
M.7.RP.A.2.cc_emerging: I can complete a simple ratio table, such as 1 box has 4 pens, 2 boxes have 8 pens, using objects or pictures.
M.7.RP.A.2.ee_at_target: I can use a ratio to describe or model a relationship.

M.7.NS.A.3.cc_advanced: I can solve multi-step real-world problems with positive and negative fractions and decimals and explain whether my answer makes sense.
M.7.NS.A.3.cc_at_target: I can add, subtract, multiply and divide rational numbers to solve real-world and math problems. Example: The temperature is -3°C and drops 4.5°C, so it is -7.5°C.
M.7.NS.A.3.cc_approaching: I can solve one-step problems with integers or simple fractions and decimals using a number line or a model.
M.7.NS.A.3.cc_emerging: I can add and subtract whole numbers and simple fractions in word problems with support.
M.7.NS.A.3.ee_at_target: I can compare decimal amounts to tenths in real-world examples.

M.7.EE.B.4.cc_advanced: I can write and solve equations and inequalities for real-world problems, compare an algebraic and an arithmetic solution, and explain what my answer means.
M.7.EE.B.4.cc_at_target: I can solve word problems with equations like px + q = r or p(x + q) = r and inequalities like px + q > r, and graph the solution. Example: 2w + 12 = 54, so w = 21.
M.7.EE.B.4.cc_approaching: I can solve two-step equations with whole numbers using a model or a step-by-step guide.
M.7.EE.B.4.cc_emerging: I can solve one-step equations like x + 5 = 12 using objects, a balance model or a bar model.
M.7.EE.B.4.ee_at_target: I can use models to solve one-step addition and subtraction equations by keeping both sides equal.

M.7.G.B.4.cc_advanced: I can use the circle formulas to solve multi-step real-world problems and explain how the area and circumference of a circle are related.
M.7.G.B.4.cc_at_target: I can use C = πd (or 2πr) and A = πr² to find the circumference and area of a circle. Example: r = 3 cm, A ≈ 3.14 × 9 = 28.26 cm².
M.7.G.B.4.cc_approaching: I can find the circumference or area of a circle when I am given the formula and the radius or diameter.
M.7.G.B.4.cc_emerging: I can find the radius and diameter of a circle and measure them with a ruler with support.
M.7.G.B.4.ee_at_target: I can find the perimeter of a rectangle.

M.7.SP.A.2.cc_advanced: I can take several random samples, compare their results, and explain how far off my estimate or prediction about the population might be.
M.7.SP.A.2.cc_at_target: I can use data from a random sample to make an estimate or prediction about a population. Example: 12 of 30 students chose red, so about 40% of the school might choose red.
M.7.SP.A.2.cc_approaching: I can use a sample to make a simple prediction about a group when I am given the data and sentence frames.
M.7.SP.A.2.cc_emerging: I can read a simple table or bar graph of survey results and say which choice was most popular with support.
M.7.SP.A.2.ee_at_target: I can answer a question about data from an experiment or collection using a model of the data.

M.7.SP.C.6.cc_advanced: I can run an experiment, compare the results to the expected probability, and explain why the results are close to, but not exactly, what I predicted.
M.7.SP.C.6.cc_at_target: I can use data from repeated trials to estimate a probability and predict how often an outcome will happen. Example: Roll a cube 600 times, a 3 or 6 should come up about 200 times.
M.7.SP.C.6.cc_approaching: I can collect data from a simple experiment, like flipping a coin, and say about how often an outcome happened with support.
M.7.SP.C.6.cc_emerging: I can say whether an event is likely or unlikely using simple chance activities.
M.7.SP.C.6.ee_at_target: I can describe whether an event is possible or impossible.

M.8.NS.A.2.cc_advanced: I can find closer and closer decimal approximations of irrational numbers and use them to compare and order expressions, explaining my process.
M.8.NS.A.2.cc_at_target: I can estimate irrational numbers with decimals, place them on a number line and compare them. Example: √2 is between 1.4 and 1.5 because 1.4² = 1.96 and 1.5² = 2.25.
M.8.NS.A.2.cc_approaching: I can find the two whole numbers a square root is between, using a list of perfect squares.
M.8.NS.A.2.cc_emerging: I can place whole numbers and simple decimals on a number line with support.
M.8.NS.A.2.ee_at_target: I can write a fraction with a denominator of 100 as a decimal and compare decimal amounts to hundredths in real-world examples.

M.8.EE.A.4.cc_advanced: I can use scientific notation and technology to solve real-world problems with very large or small numbers and explain which units are sensible.
M.8.EE.A.4.cc_at_target: I can use technology to calculate with numbers in scientific notation, read the results, and choose sensible units for very large or small amounts. Example: (3 × 10⁴) × (2 × 10³) = 6 × 10⁷.
M.8.EE.A.4.cc_approaching: I can write a number in scientific notation and read a calculator result in scientific notation with support.
M.8.EE.A.4.cc_emerging: I can multiply and divide whole numbers by 10, 100 and 1,000 using a place value chart.
M.8.EE.A.4.ee_at_target: I can build and break apart whole numbers up to 999.

M.8.EE.C.8.cc_advanced: I can write and solve systems of two linear equations for real-world problems and explain what the solution, or no solution, means in the situation.
M.8.EE.C.8.cc_at_target: I can solve a system of two linear equations by graphing or tables and know the solution is where the lines meet. Example: y = x + 1 and y = 3 meet at (2, 3).
M.8.EE.C.8.cc_approaching: I can graph two lines and find the point where they cross using a table of values with support.
M.8.EE.C.8.cc_emerging: I can complete a table of values for one simple equation and plot the points.

M.8.F.B.4.cc_advanced: I can build a linear function for a real-world situation and explain what its rate of change and initial value mean in the context and on the graph.
M.8.F.B.4.cc_at_target: I can find the rate of change and initial value from a description, table, graph or two points and write a linear function. Example: $5 plus $2 per hour is y = 2x + 5.
M.8.F.B.4.cc_approaching: I can find the rate of change and starting value from a table or graph with support.
M.8.F.B.4.cc_emerging: I can describe a growing pattern in a table, such as "add 2 each time".
M.8.F.B.4.ee_at_target: I can find the values or rule of a function from a graph or table.

M.8.G.A.3.cc_advanced: I can predict and explain how a sequence of transformations changes the coordinates of a figure.
M.8.G.A.3.cc_at_target: I can describe how translations, rotations, reflections and dilations change a figure's coordinates. Example: Reflecting (3, 2) over the x-axis gives (3, -2).
M.8.G.A.3.cc_approaching: I can perform a translation or reflection on a grid and list the new coordinates with support.
M.8.G.A.3.cc_emerging: I can slide, flip or turn a shape on a grid using cut-outs or tracing paper.

M.8.G.B.7.cc_advanced: I can use the Pythagorean Theorem to solve multi-step real-world problems in two and three dimensions and explain my steps.
M.8.G.B.7.cc_at_target: I can use a² + b² = c² to find a missing side of a right triangle in real-world and math problems. Example: legs 6 and 8, so c = √100 = 10.
M.8.G.B.7.cc_approaching: I can find the hypotenuse of a right triangle with whole number sides using the formula and a calculator.
M.8.G.B.7.cc_emerging: I can find the square of a number and identify the right angle and longest side of a right triangle with support.

M.8.SP.A.2.cc_advanced: I can fit a line to a scatter plot, judge how well it fits, and explain why one line is a better model than another.
M.8.SP.A.2.cc_at_target: I can draw a straight line that fits a scatter plot with a linear pattern and judge how close the points are to the line.
M.8.SP.A.2.cc_approaching: I can tell if a scatter plot shows a linear pattern and draw a line close to the points with support.
M.8.SP.A.2.cc_emerging: I can plot points from a table on a graph with help.

M.N.RN.A.2.cc_advanced: I can rewrite complex expressions with radicals and rational exponents in simplest form and explain which exponent properties I used.
M.N.RN.A.2.cc_at_target: I can rewrite expressions between radical and rational exponent form using properties of exponents. Example: x^(1/2) = √x and 8^(2/3) = 4.
M.N.RN.A.2.cc_approaching: I can change simple expressions like x^(1/2) to √x using a reference chart.
M.N.RN.A.2.cc_emerging: I can find square roots and cube roots of perfect squares and cubes with support.

M.N.Q.A.3.cc_advanced: I can explain how the tool I use limits accuracy and decide on a sensible level of precision for a real-world calculation.
M.N.Q.A.3.cc_at_target: I can report a measurement or answer with a level of accuracy that fits the measuring tool. Example: A ruler marked in mm gives 12.4 cm, not 12.4378 cm.
M.N.Q.A.3.cc_approaching: I can round a measurement to a given place value when I am told how accurate it should be.
M.N.Q.A.3.cc_emerging: I can measure an object to the nearest whole unit with a ruler with support.
M.N.Q.A.3.ee_at_target: I can express quantities with a precise measurement based on the context.

M.N.CN.B.4.cc_advanced: I can convert complex numbers between rectangular and polar form and explain why both forms name the same number.
M.N.CN.B.4.cc_at_target: I can plot complex numbers on the complex plane in rectangular and polar form. Example: 1 + i is (√2, 45°) in polar form.
M.N.CN.B.4.cc_approaching: I can plot a complex number a + bi on the complex plane and find its distance from the origin with support.
M.N.CN.B.4.cc_emerging: I can plot points on a coordinate plane and find the distance from the origin using the Pythagorean Theorem.

M.N.CN.C.8.cc_advanced: I can use complex numbers to factor sums of squares and other polynomials and check my factors by multiplying.
M.N.CN.C.8.cc_at_target: I can extend polynomial identities to complex numbers. Example: x² + 4 = (x + 2i)(x - 2i).
M.N.CN.C.8.cc_approaching: I can factor simple expressions like x² + 9 using a worked example and the fact that i² = -1.
M.N.CN.C.8.cc_emerging: I can factor a difference of squares like x² - 9 = (x + 3)(x - 3) with support.

M.N.VM.A.3.cc_advanced: I can model multi-step real-world situations, such as a boat in a current, with vectors and explain what the resultant vector means.
M.N.VM.A.3.cc_at_target: I can solve problems about velocity and other quantities using vectors. Example: A plane flying 300 km/h north with a 40 km/h east wind has speed √(300² + 40²) ≈ 303 km/h.
M.N.VM.A.3.cc_approaching: I can add two vectors using a diagram and find the resultant with support.
M.N.VM.A.3.cc_emerging: I can draw a vector as an arrow showing size and direction.

M.N.VM.C.7.cc_advanced: I can use scalar multiplication of matrices to solve real-world problems and explain what the new matrix means.
M.N.VM.C.7.cc_at_target: I can multiply a matrix by a scalar to make a new matrix. Example: 2 × [1 3; 4 0] = [2 6; 8 0].
M.N.VM.C.7.cc_approaching: I can multiply each entry of a small matrix by a whole number with support.
M.N.VM.C.7.cc_emerging: I can read entries in a table by row and column.

M.N.VM.C.11.cc_advanced: I can use a matrix to transform vectors, such as rotating or reflecting points, and explain the effect of the transformation.
M.N.VM.C.11.cc_at_target: I can multiply a vector by a matrix of the right size to get a new vector and see the matrix as a transformation. Example: [0 -1; 1 0] times (1, 0) gives (0, 1).
M.N.VM.C.11.cc_approaching: I can multiply a 2 × 2 matrix by a vector using a step-by-step guide.
M.N.VM.C.11.cc_emerging: I can multiply and add pairs of numbers in order, such as (2 × 3) + (1 × 4).

M.A.SSE.B.3.cc_advanced: I can choose the best form of an expression, factored, vertex or exponential, to answer a real-world question and explain what the form shows.
M.A.SSE.B.3.cc_at_target: I can factor quadratics to find zeros, complete the square to find a maximum or minimum, and rewrite exponential expressions. Example: x² - 5x + 6 = (x - 2)(x - 3), zeros 2 and 3.
M.A.SSE.B.3.cc_approaching: I can factor simple quadratics with a leading coefficient of 1 and find the zeros with support.
M.A.SSE.B.3.cc_emerging: I can find two numbers that multiply to one number and add to another, using a factor list.
M.A.SSE.B.3.ee_at_target: I can solve simple one-variable equations using multiplication and division.

M.A.APR.B.3.cc_advanced: I can find zeros of a polynomial, use them and end behavior to sketch its graph, and explain how multiplicity affects the graph.
M.A.APR.B.3.cc_at_target: I can find the zeros of a factored polynomial and use them to sketch a rough graph. Example: y = (x - 1)(x + 2) crosses the x-axis at 1 and -2.
M.A.APR.B.3.cc_approaching: I can find the zeros of a polynomial that is already factored and mark them on the x-axis.
M.A.APR.B.3.cc_emerging: I can solve simple equations like x - 3 = 0 and plot points on the x-axis.

M.A.APR.D.7.cc_advanced: I can add, subtract, multiply and divide complex rational expressions, simplify fully, and explain why they behave like rational numbers.
M.A.APR.D.7.cc_at_target: I can add, subtract, multiply and divide rational expressions and simplify the result. Example: 1/x + 2/x = 3/x.
M.A.APR.D.7.cc_approaching: I can add or multiply simple rational expressions with the same denominator using a worked example.
M.A.APR.D.7.cc_emerging: I can add, subtract, multiply and divide numerical fractions.

M.A.CED.A.4.cc_advanced: I can rearrange multi-step formulas from science or real life to solve for any variable and explain each step.
M.A.CED.A.4.cc_at_target: I can rearrange a formula to solve for a chosen quantity, using the same steps as solving equations. Example: C = 5/9(F - 32) becomes F = 9/5C + 32.
M.A.CED.A.4.cc_approaching: I can rearrange simple formulas like A = lw to solve for one variable with support.
M.A.CED.A.4.cc_emerging: I can solve one-step equations using inverse operations.

M.A.REI.B.4.cc_advanced: I can choose the most efficient method to solve any quadratic equation, explain my choice, and write complex solutions as a ± bi.
M.A.REI.B.4.cc_at_target: I can solve quadratic equations by square roots, factoring, completing the square, the quadratic formula or graphing. Example: x² = 49, so x = 7 or x = -7.
M.A.REI.B.4.cc_approaching: I can solve quadratic equations by taking square roots or by using the quadratic formula with a step-by-step guide.
M.A.REI.B.4.cc_emerging: I can solve simple equations like x² = 25 using a list of perfect squares.

M.A.REI.C.8.cc_advanced: I can write a system of linear equations as a matrix equation and explain how each part of the matrix equation matches the system.
M.A.REI.C.8.cc_at_target: I can write a system of linear equations as one matrix equation AX = B. Example: 2x + y = 5 and x - y = 1 becomes [2 1; 1 -1][x; y] = [5; 1].
M.A.REI.C.8.cc_approaching: I can pick out the coefficients and constants of a system and place them in a matrix with support.
M.A.REI.C.8.cc_emerging: I can identify the coefficient and constant in a linear equation.

M.A.REI.D.12.cc_advanced: I can graph a system of linear inequalities for a real-world problem and explain which points in the solution region make sense.
M.A.REI.D.12.cc_at_target: I can graph the solutions of a linear inequality as a half-plane, using a dashed line for < or >, and find where two half-planes overlap. Example: y > x + 1 has a dashed line and shading above.
M.A.REI.D.12.cc_approaching: I can graph the boundary line of an inequality and shade the correct side by testing a point with support.
M.A.REI.D.12.cc_emerging: I can graph a linear equation from a table of values.
M.A.REI.D.12.ee_at_target: I can explain what a point on the graph of a line means, such as the number of pizzas bought and their total cost.

M.F.IF.B.4.cc_advanced: I can sketch a graph from a description of a real-world relationship and explain how its key features match the situation.
M.F.IF.B.4.cc_at_target: I can interpret key features of graphs and tables, such as intercepts, increasing or decreasing intervals, maximums, minimums, symmetry and end behavior, in terms of the situation.
M.F.IF.B.4.cc_approaching: I can identify intercepts and where a graph is increasing or decreasing using a labeled graph and sentence frames.
M.F.IF.B.4.cc_emerging: I can read values from a graph and say whether it goes up or down with support.
M.F.IF.B.4.ee_at_target: I can graph linear functions with different rates of change and explain which rate is faster or slower.

M.F.IF.C.8.cc_advanced: I can rewrite quadratic and exponential functions in different forms and explain what each form shows about a real-world situation.
M.F.IF.C.8.cc_at_target: I can rewrite quadratics in vertex or factored form to find key features, and rewrite exponential functions to find percent rates of change. Example: y = 1.2^(t/10) means 20% growth each decade.
M.F.IF.C.8.cc_approaching: I can find the zeros or vertex of a quadratic from a given form and identify growth or decay in an exponential function with support.
M.F.IF.C.8.cc_emerging: I can factor simple quadratics and tell if a number above or below 1 means growth or decay.

M.F.BF.B.3.cc_advanced: I can predict and explain the effect of combined transformations on a graph and decide if a function is even or odd from its graph and its equation.
M.F.BF.B.3.cc_at_target: I can describe how f(x) + k, k·f(x), f(kx) and f(x + k) change a graph and find k from two graphs. Example: f(x) + 3 moves the graph up 3.
M.F.BF.B.3.cc_approaching: I can use technology to see how adding a number shifts a graph up, down, left or right with support.
M.F.BF.B.3.cc_emerging: I can graph a simple function from a table and compare two graphs.

M.F.LE.A.2.cc_advanced: I can decide if a real-world situation is linear or exponential, build the function, and explain what each part means.
M.F.LE.A.2.cc_at_target: I can write linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences, from a graph, a description, a table or two points. Example: 3, 6, 12, 24 is f(n) = 3·2^(n-1).
M.F.LE.A.2.cc_approaching: I can write a linear function from a table or an arithmetic sequence with support.
M.F.LE.A.2.cc_emerging: I can find the pattern in a sequence, such as add 4 or multiply by 2.
M.F.LE.A.2.ee_at_target: I can model a simple linear function like y = mx and show it increases by equal amounts over equal intervals.

M.F.TF.A.1.cc_advanced: I can convert between degrees and radians and explain how the radian measure connects to arc length on the unit circle.
M.F.TF.A.1.cc_at_target: I can explain that the radian measure of an angle is the length of the arc it cuts on the unit circle. Example: A half turn is π radians.
M.F.TF.A.1.cc_approaching: I can identify common radian measures, like π and π/2, on a unit circle diagram.
M.F.TF.A.1.cc_emerging: I can find the circumference of a circle and measure angles in degrees.

M.F.TF.B.5.cc_advanced: I can model a real-world periodic situation, such as tides, with a trigonometric function and explain how amplitude, frequency and midline match the data.
M.F.TF.B.5.cc_at_target: I can choose a sine or cosine function to model a periodic situation with a given amplitude, frequency and midline. Example: y = 3sin(2x) + 5 has amplitude 3 and midline y = 5.
M.F.TF.B.5.cc_approaching: I can identify the amplitude and midline of a sine or cosine graph with support.
M.F.TF.B.5.cc_emerging: I can recognize a repeating pattern in a graph or table.

M.F.TF.C.9.cc_advanced: I can prove the addition and subtraction formulas for sine, cosine and tangent and use them to solve multi-step problems.
M.F.TF.C.9.cc_at_target: I can prove the addition and subtraction formulas for sine, cosine and tangent and use them to find exact values. Example: sin(75°) = sin45°cos30° + cos45°sin30°.
M.F.TF.C.9.cc_approaching: I can use the addition formulas to find exact values when I am given the formula.
M.F.TF.C.9.cc_emerging: I can find sine, cosine and tangent of special angles using the unit circle with support.

M.G.CO.A.4.cc_advanced: I can write precise definitions of rotations, reflections and translations and use them to explain why a transformation works.
M.G.CO.A.4.cc_at_target: I can define rotations, reflections and translations using angles, circles, perpendicular lines, parallel lines and line segments.
M.G.CO.A.4.cc_approaching: I can describe a rotation, reflection or translation using words from a word bank and a diagram.
M.G.CO.A.4.cc_emerging: I can slide, flip and turn shapes and name each move with support.
M.G.CO.A.4.ee_at_target: I can identify the parts of a figure and its rotation, reflection or translation that are congruent.

M.G.CO.B.8.cc_advanced: I can use rigid motions to justify ASA, SAS and SSS and explain why other combinations, like SSA, do not prove congruence.
M.G.CO.B.8.cc_at_target: I can explain how ASA, SAS and SSS follow from the definition of congruence using rigid motions.
M.G.CO.B.8.cc_approaching: I can identify which congruence rule, ASA, SAS or SSS, shows two triangles are congruent using marked diagrams.
M.G.CO.B.8.cc_emerging: I can match equal sides and equal angles in two triangles with support.
M.G.CO.B.8.ee_at_target: I can identify corresponding congruent and similar parts of shapes.

M.G.CO.D.12.cc_advanced: I can choose a construction method to solve a problem, such as finding the center of a circle, and explain why the construction works.
M.G.CO.D.12.cc_at_target: I can use tools like a compass and straightedge to copy segments and angles, bisect them, and construct perpendicular and parallel lines.
M.G.CO.D.12.cc_approaching: I can complete a construction, such as bisecting a segment, by following step-by-step pictures.
M.G.CO.D.12.cc_emerging: I can use a ruler and compass to draw segments and circles with support.

M.G.SRT.A.3.cc_advanced: I can use similarity transformations to prove the AA criterion and apply it to show triangles are similar in real-world problems.
M.G.SRT.A.3.cc_at_target: I can use similarity transformations to explain why two triangles with two pairs of equal angles are similar (AA).
M.G.SRT.A.3.cc_approaching: I can identify similar triangles by finding two pairs of equal angles in a diagram.
M.G.SRT.A.3.cc_emerging: I can measure angles and tell if two shapes look the same but are different sizes.

M.G.SRT.C.7.cc_advanced: I can use the relationship between sine and cosine of complementary angles to solve problems and explain why it is true using a right triangle.
M.G.SRT.C.7.cc_at_target: I can explain and use the fact that the sine of an angle equals the cosine of its complement. Example: sin 30° = cos 60°.
M.G.SRT.C.7.cc_approaching: I can find sine and cosine of the two acute angles in a right triangle and notice they swap.
M.G.SRT.C.7.cc_emerging: I can identify complementary angles that add to 90° with support.

M.G.SRT.D.11.cc_advanced: I can choose the Law of Sines or the Law of Cosines to solve real-world problems, such as surveying, and explain my choice.
M.G.SRT.D.11.cc_at_target: I can use the Law of Sines and the Law of Cosines to find unknown sides and angles in any triangle. Example: c² = a² + b² - 2ab·cos C.
M.G.SRT.D.11.cc_approaching: I can use the Law of Sines or the Law of Cosines when I am told which one to use and given the formula.
M.G.SRT.D.11.cc_emerging: I can use sine, cosine and tangent to find a missing side in a right triangle with support.

M.G.GPE.A.2.cc_advanced: I can derive the equation of a parabola with any focus and directrix and explain how the definition leads to the equation.
M.G.GPE.A.2.cc_at_target: I can derive the equation of a parabola from its focus and directrix using the distance formula. Example: focus (0, 1) and directrix y = -1 give x² = 4y.
M.G.GPE.A.2.cc_approaching: I can find the equation of a parabola with its vertex at the origin using a step-by-step guide.
M.G.GPE.A.2.cc_emerging: I can use the distance formula to find the distance between two points.

M.G.GPE.B.6.cc_advanced: I can partition segments in any ratio to solve real-world problems, such as locating a point on a map, and explain my method.
M.G.GPE.B.6.cc_at_target: I can find the point on a directed line segment that divides it in a given ratio. Example: From (0, 0) to (6, 9) in ratio 1:2, the point is (2, 3).
M.G.GPE.B.6.cc_approaching: I can find the midpoint of a segment and a point that divides a horizontal or vertical segment in a simple ratio with support.
M.G.GPE.B.6.cc_emerging: I can find the length of a horizontal or vertical segment on a grid.

M.G.GMD.B.3.cc_advanced: I can predict and explain the 3D shape formed when a 2D shape is rotated around different lines.
M.G.GMD.B.3.cc_at_target: I can identify the 3D object made when a 2D shape is rotated around a line. Example: Rotating a rectangle around one side makes a cylinder.
M.G.GMD.B.3.cc_approaching: I can match a 2D shape to the 3D object it makes when rotated, using pictures or models.
M.G.GMD.B.3.cc_emerging: I can name common 2D and 3D shapes with support.

M.SP.ID.A.1.cc_advanced: I can choose the best plot, dot plot, histogram or box plot, for a data set and explain what it shows about the data.
M.SP.ID.A.1.cc_at_target: I can display data on a number line using dot plots, histograms and box plots.
M.SP.ID.A.1.cc_approaching: I can make a dot plot or histogram from a small data set using a given scale.
M.SP.ID.A.1.cc_emerging: I can sort and count data and make a simple picture or bar graph with support.
M.SP.ID.A.1.ee_at_target: I can make a graph or table from data and interpret the data.

M.SP.ID.B.5.cc_advanced: I can use relative frequencies in a two-way table to describe associations in data and explain whether they suggest a trend.
M.SP.ID.B.5.cc_at_target: I can make a two-way frequency table, find joint, marginal and conditional relative frequencies, and describe possible associations. Example: 18 of 30 girls chose soccer, so 60%.
M.SP.ID.B.5.cc_approaching: I can complete a two-way table and find the totals for each row and column with support.
M.SP.ID.B.5.cc_emerging: I can sort data into categories and count each group.

M.SP.ID.C.9.cc_advanced: I can explain why a correlation does not prove causation and suggest another factor that could explain a relationship.
M.SP.ID.C.9.cc_at_target: I can tell the difference between correlation and causation. Example: Taller children read better, but height does not cause reading ability. Age affects both.
M.SP.ID.C.9.cc_approaching: I can say whether two things are related in a data set and decide if one causes the other with sentence frames.
M.SP.ID.C.9.cc_emerging: I can describe whether two quantities go up together using a picture or graph with support.

M.SP.IC.B.4.cc_advanced: I can use simulations to find a margin of error and explain how sample size affects how accurate an estimate is.
M.SP.IC.B.4.cc_at_target: I can use sample survey data to estimate a population mean or proportion and use simulations to find a margin of error.
M.SP.IC.B.4.cc_approaching: I can find the mean or proportion of a sample and use it to estimate for the whole population with support.
M.SP.IC.B.4.cc_emerging: I can find the mean of a small data set and the fraction of a group that chose an option.

M.SP.CP.A.2.cc_advanced: I can use probabilities from real-world data to decide if two events are independent and explain my reasoning.
M.SP.CP.A.2.cc_at_target: I can decide if events A and B are independent by checking if P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B). Example: A coin and a die: P(heads and 6) = 1/2 × 1/6 = 1/12.
M.SP.CP.A.2.cc_approaching: I can multiply probabilities of two independent events, like coin flips, using a tree diagram or table.
M.SP.CP.A.2.cc_emerging: I can find the probability of a simple event, such as rolling a 3, as a fraction.
M.SP.CP.A.2.ee_at_target: I can identify when events are independent or dependent.

M.SP.CP.B.6.cc_advanced: I can find conditional probabilities from two-way tables or Venn diagrams in real-world contexts and explain what they mean.
M.SP.CP.B.6.cc_at_target: I can use a two-way table or Venn diagram to find the probability of A given B as the fraction of B's outcomes that are also in A. Example: 12 of 40 in B are in A, so 12/40 = 0.3.
M.SP.CP.B.6.cc_approaching: I can find a conditional probability from a two-way table when the correct row or column is highlighted.
M.SP.CP.B.6.cc_emerging: I can read counts from a two-way table or Venn diagram with support.

M.SP.MD.A.1.cc_advanced: I can define a random variable for a real-world situation, graph its probability distribution, and describe what the graph shows.
M.SP.MD.A.1.cc_at_target: I can assign a number to each outcome in a sample space and graph the probability distribution. Example: Number of heads in 2 coin flips: P(0) = 1/4, P(1) = 1/2, P(2) = 1/4.
M.SP.MD.A.1.cc_approaching: I can list outcomes of a simple experiment and find the probability of each value with support.
M.SP.MD.A.1.cc_emerging: I can list all the outcomes of a simple event, like flipping a coin twice.

M.SP.MD.B.5.cc_advanced: I can compare decisions or strategies, such as insurance plans, using expected values and explain which choice is better and why.
M.SP.MD.B.5.cc_at_target: I can find the expected value of a game or decision by multiplying each payoff by its probability and adding. Example: Win $10 with 1/5 chance, else $0: expected value = $2.
M.SP.MD.B.5.cc_approaching: I can find the expected value of a simple game when the payoffs and probabilities are given in a table.
M.SP.MD.B.5.cc_emerging: I can find the probability of simple events and multiply a fraction by a whole number.
